title: Edge Control Plane Commissioning: Workflow & TF Compatibility (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for commissioning small-footprint control planes placed at the edge (customer colo / remote VPCs) with an emphasis on: terraform compatibility across environments, a minimal commissioning workflow, safe upgrade trajectories for controlplane components, and rotation/evacuation patterns for resource-constrained clusters.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: SREs, Platform engineers responsible for private CP installs, and Solutions Eng for field handoffs.
- Scope: initial provisioning steps -> acceptance tests -> scale/rotation patterns -> upgrade plan -> common rollback scenarios. Not a final runbook; complements the main runbook bucket.

Summary of approach:
1) Keep TF state and modules stable: pin providers and module versions in a thin wrapper module (module: cp-edge-wrapper).
2) Commission in three phases: prep (infra + secrets), bootstrap (controlplane core + minimal services), validate & scale (observability + occupancy adjustments).
3) Upgrades use a staged canary approach within customer boundaries: single-node canary -> partial rollout -> full rollout with automatic fallback.

Prereqs (high level):
- Customer network: IP ranges, VPN/BGP config, firewall ACLs, outbound egress for metrics and KMS endpoints.
- KMS/HSM access for keys: ensure CMKs are provisioned and accessible from the controlplane subnet.
- TF remote state: s3/gs:// or customer-managed backend with locking (dynamodb/terraform-cloud) configured.
- Operator access: service account keys and brief credentials handed to on-call for deploys.

Quick commissioning workflow (steps):
PREP (day 0)
- Collect network facts: CIDR allocations, NAT gateway info, control plane bastion IPs.
- Confirm DNS plan: internal names, wildcard certs, or Let's Encrypt alternatives if allowed.
- Create remote state bucket and locking table.
- Create minimal secrets skeleton in the target KMS (key aliases use cp-edge-<customer>-key).

TERRAFORM WRAPPER (local repo layout)
- repo: infra/edge-cp/<customer>/main.tf (thin wrapper)
- file: versions.tf pins provider versions (aws v4.60.0, google v4.x, kubernetes v2.x depending on cloud)
- module: module "cp-edge" { source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-controlplane-modules//edge?ref=v2.1.0" }
- workflow: terraform init -> plan (with -var-file=secrets.tfvars) -> apply (with -parallelism=10)

Module compatibility notes (collected gotchas):
- aws provider: older edge customers sometimes run provider < 4.56 which changed iam role import behavior; our modules use iamv2 assumptions. Pin provider in module or include shim variables.
- kubernetes provider: API differences across k8s 1.22->1.27; in small edge installs we currently target K8s 1.24+; ensure provider accepts kubeconfig timeout overrides.
- helm provider: chart values schema changed for the metrics agent between v0.3 and v0.5. Bundle a locked chart archive in the module to avoid remote fetch mismatches.
- resource naming: modules now enforce a 32-char limit; older customer naming templates exceed this and cause apply failures. Document the truncation strategy.

Bootstrap apply hints:
- Use terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan and store the plan artifact for audit.
- For noisy resources (instance pools, node groups) set lifecycle.create_before_destroy = true where possible to reduce downtime.
- Set apply -parallelism to limit API burst if customer APIs rate-limit.

Minimal bootstrap checklist (hand-executable):
- [ ] Confirm remote state accessible and locking ok
- [ ] KMS keys exist and test decrypt/ encrypt with the service account
- [ ] DNS entries reserved or CNAME plan ready
- [ ] Run terraform plan and review for unexpected destroys
- [ ] terraform apply (monitor logs and events)
- [ ] Smoke: controlplane API responds on port 8443, health /version returns expected bundle

Post-bootstrap validation (automated & manual):
Automated tests (CI snippets available in infra/tests/edge):
- controlplane health: GET https://<cp-host>/healthz -> 200 in <10s
- KV-store sync: check raft/quorum size (if using embedded or etcd managed module)
- KV cache warm: a few synthetic requests to validate KV cache hits
Manual checks:
- Confirm TLS cert chain is valid and matches wildcard
- Confirm logs flow to customer-approved observability endpoint (or to Redwood agent if configured)

Scaling & rotation patterns for edge clusters:
- Small installs (<=3 worker nodes): prefer vertical scaling (bigger instance types) over horizontal to minimize orchestration churn.
- Medium installs (3-10 nodes): prefer scheduled batch rotations during low traffic windows with canary instance first.
- Large installs (>10 nodes): rolling update with parallelism=2 and health probes to gate progress.

Rotation checklist (nodes & secrets):
- Node rotation (TF-driven nodepool replace):
  1) Mark one node drain=true in cluster admin
  2) Wait for pods to reschedule and check PDBs
  3) terraform apply to replace instance (ensure create_before_destroy)
  4) Verify metrics and remove evicted taints
- Secret/KMS rotation (CMK rotate/fallback pattern):
  1) Stage new key (rotate-key alias->new-key) and grant decrypt to service accounts
  2) Re-encrypt small test object to validate access
  3) Update TF var linking to new key ARN and run plan/apply against a non-critical module (e.g., agent config)
  4) Monitor for decrypt errors for 24-72 hours before retiring old key

Upgrade plan (controlplane components):
Principles:
- Always canary one instance/component first and wait for full telemetry/QA window before continuing.
- Keep a quick rollback path (image pin, terraform apply with previous tag).
Phases:
1) Canary image -> patch deployment on single replica (or single az)
2) Monitor for 4h (metrics: error-rate, p95 latency, cpu, mem, restart-count)
3) If green, proceed to 20% of nodes; repeat monitoring window 2h
4) Gradual rollout to 100% with 1-hour gating windows between each increment for edge installs
Rollback triggers:
- error-rate increase > 2x baseline for >10m
- p95 latency regressed beyond SLOs
- crashloop/restart count suddenly non-zero for critical pods
Actions on trigger:
- Immediately promote previous image tag in the deployment with kubectl set image or via terraform module image var and apply
- If image rollback fails, toggle network isolation for canary and route traffic to fallback region/provider (if configured)

Evacuation & full-swap scenario (worst case)
- Use case: underlying hardware or network has persistent failure, need to create new controlplane in alternate VPC/colo and remap DNS.
Steps:
1) Provision new controlplane with same config in alternate land (use plan artifact + var-file to reproduce)
2) Validate stateful sync (KV snapshot import/export) - take final snapshot from old cluster and import into new one
3) Switch DNS TTL low beforehand and perform DNS cutover once validations pass
4) Monitor telemetry and preserve old cluster for 24h in read-only mode before termination

Common rollback scenarios (examples & commands):
- Terraform drift caused nodepool to be destroyed: restore from plan artifact and re-apply with -target=module.nodepool["primary"] to recreate
- Helm chart incompatible change: helm rollback <release> <revision> or replace chart with previous locked artifact in module source

Telemetry & SLOs to track during commissioning and upgrades:
- API p95 latency (SLO: <300ms for control operations)
- Auth errors / 5xx rate (SLO: <0.1% sustained)
- KV replication lag (SLO: <1s typical for small clusters)
- Agent telemetry ingestion rate and backlog size
- Terraform apply durations and failure rates for audit

Housekeeping & artifacts to capture:
- Save terraform plan artifacts and associate with ticket/PR
- Export kube manifests of deployed critical services (kubectl get deploy -o yaml) to artifact store
- Capture KMS key rotation timeline in a short changelog entry and attach to the customer onboarding doc

Known risky areas & mitigations:
- Provider version skews: mitigate by bundling provider constraints in wrapper and gating upgrades in CI with a smoke cluster
- Resource name truncation issues: run name-sanity checks pre-plan and fail-fast with a descriptive message
- Network flakiness: use conservative apply parallelism and longer timeouts in providers

Open questions / TODOs (tracked for next pass):
- Decide default K8s version for edge installs and pin in module policy (proposal: 1.25 as baseline)
- Add an optional "lightbox" mode that uses a sqlite-backed local store for ultra-small installs (tradeoffs need review)
- Automate CMK handoff via short-lived delegation tokens instead of static TF vars

Appendix: useful commands & snippets
- Test KMS decrypt: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id alias/cp-edge-demo --profile customer
- Plan with var-file: terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan
- Apply with lock: terraform apply "plan.tfplan"

Contacts & escalation
- Primary eng owner: Maya Alvarez (oncall rotation: eng-private-deployments)
- Backup: Samir Patel
- Solutions lead for field installs: Jules Fischer

This doc should be iterated after the next two field installs; use the checklist items above to create short playbooks for the onboarding team.
